# Ragdoll

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- Created with `Instance.new("Ragdoll")`

Makes a character's pose follow the physics simulation instead of an animation. Parent it to the skinned `MeshPart`, put the limb parts under it, and enable it.

A ragdoll is made of ordinary instances: a `Part` for each limb, a `Bone` on each part that names the joint the part drives, and constraints between the parts. `Ragdoll` only tells the engine to take the pose from them. Every `Bone` under the ragdoll that names a joint and sits on a part drives that joint.

Joints that no bone drives keep their place relative to their parent, so a partial ragdoll works: simulate a dozen joints and the fingers follow the wrist.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Blend` | `number` | `1` | read/write | How much of the pose comes from the simulation, from 0 (none) to 1 (all).<br><br>The blend is between two poses: each driven joint is drawn between where the animation puts it and where its limb part is. It does not weaken the simulation; the limb parts fall the same way at any value. Ramp it from 0 to 1 over a few tenths of a second to make a character go down without a visible snap, and back to 0 to make it get up. |
| `Enabled` | `boolean` | `false` | read/write | Whether the pose comes from the simulation. Turning it off returns the character to the animation that is playing, from the next tick. |

## Methods

### `Build(profile: { any }): number`

Creates the limbs of the ragdoll from a profile and returns how many it made. For each joint the profile names, it creates a `Part`, a `Bone` on the part that names the joint, and a constraint to the limb above. The limbs are created at the rig's current pose.

Everything it creates is an ordinary instance that you can select, move, adjust and delete. Run it once in the editor and save the scene, and the ragdoll is part of the scene with no script needed.

A profile is an ordered list of limbs. `require("@engine/ragdoll").Humanoid` is a built-in profile that fits common humanoid rigs. Each entry is a table:

- `Joint`: the joint's name, or a list of names tried in order.
- `Parent`: the 1-based index of the limb this one hangs from; omit it for the root. It must refer to an earlier entry.
- `Radius`, `LeafLength`: the capsule's radius, and the length of a limb that has nothing below it. Otherwise a limb's length is the distance to the joint below it.
- `Kind`: `"BallSocket"`, `"Hinge"` or `"Fixed"`.
- `Swing`, `Twist`: for a ball socket, the cone half-angle and the twist range, in degrees.
- `LimitLow`, `LimitHigh`: for a hinge, the range in degrees.

A limb whose joint the rig does not have is skipped, and its children hang from the nearest limb that was built. Raises an error if the ragdoll is not under a skinned `MeshPart`, if it already has limbs, if the profile is malformed, or if the rig has none of the profile's joints.
